issue.description: After the decoded-view and structured-blocking review, inspect section 3.4 against bead redact behavior, accepted secret-rejection-v1, and independent synthetic range vectors using only permitted specifications and public API documentation. Acceptance: record the exact input hashes, prove or reject raw half-open range construction and redact revalidation behavior, document compatibility and threat-model consequences, and state an explicit slice decision in docs/reviews/.
issue.notes:
No repository file or commit was needed. The requested exact-hash review is already in committed docs/reviews/beadrs-db0131b7-ruleset-v4-raw-range-redact-review-2026-10-04.md; the later docs/reviews/br-t35-aggregate-compatibility-threat-decision-2026-10-04.md rechecks it against the decoded/structured review and accepts section 3.4 only for range construction and revalidation. Their exact SHA-256 input tables were rechecked unchanged, including ruleset v4, accepted secret-rejection-v1 and its R038 acceptance record, historical-redaction-v1, the public bead-redact manual, and the independent fixture inputs.

Independent harmless byte probes reconfirmed the covering-range formula. For `λpre` + one raw byte 0x5c + `u002Ffix`, the normalized `/fi` span [5,8) covers raw [5,13). For `λA` + ESC[31m + `B` + ESC[0m + `C`, normalized `BC` [3,5) covers raw [8,14). For `λAB` + bytes 0x5c, 0x0a, 0x20, 0x09 + `CD`, dewrapped `BC` [3,5) covers raw [3,9). For `!!` + base64 of `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcd` + `!`, the 40-byte run decodes to 30 benign bytes; illustrative decoded `mnopqr` [12,18) reports the entire raw run [2,42). These are mapping probes, not scanner-positive claims. The exact spec and artifact hashes and prior independent vectors are recorded in the linked review.

Decision: section 3.4's raw UTF-8 byte ranges and raw-range fingerprints are compatible with v1. `bead redact` accepts a fingerprint rather than caller offsets, resolves a retained checkpoint issue finding to its live field, revalidates under redaction locks, and conflicts on stale content; dry-run reports the effect. Whole-run decoded redaction can erase unrelated encoded content. The narrow section 3.4 slice is ACCEPTED; complete v4 compatibility/release remains REJECTED because section 3.2 leaves run selection, over-limit behavior, and decoder grammar unspecified. Revalidation cannot recover a missed finding or make divergent scanners agree. No implementation source or other implementation material was consulted.

This task staged and committed nothing. `git status --short` showed staged and unstaged work from other tasks, left untouched; checklist step 1 could not be satisfied truthfully, so the bead remains open.
